messages:
maya: heads up — p99 inference latency is spiking on shared-gpu pools in us-west-2 this morning, starting ~03:10 UTC. CPU steal high on the host and tx drops on eth0.
omar: saw that, also noticed packet drops correlated with big-batch tenants — nv_peer_mem shows high dma transfers.
raj: can you paste the query/graph? which metric for tx drops?
maya: here's the grafana link: https://grafana.redwood/… (redacted). main spike is `host.net.eth0.tx_dropped` and `node_cpu_steal`.
sylvia: my hypothesis: large batched inference from tenant X fills NIC qdisc -> kernel starts throttling, causing scheduler delays and GPU stalls. we saw similar in apac tests.
lee: if kernel softirq backlog grows, you'll get CPU steal even w/ idle cpus. do we have `tc` shaping on those hosts?
omar: not consistently. some hosts have tc ingress egress polcies but no per-tenant shaping.
maya: can we try a small experiment: eBPF-based per-cgroup tx shaping + limit large batchers to 1Gbps and observe p99?
raj: +1. also suggest forcing small kernels: `ethtool -K eth0 tso off gso off gro off` on a test pod to see if segmentation helps.
infra-bot: probe scheduled: nic-shaping-probe-2049876543 -> 5 hosts in us-west-2, start 2049876600 UTC
sylvia: runbook steps I used last time:
```
# on host
sudo tc qdisc add dev eth0 root fq_codel limit 1000
sudo cgcreate -g net_cls:tenantX
# attach cgroup to pod
echo 0x10001 > /sys/fs/cgroup/net_cls/tenantX/net_cls.classid
```
Try with fq_codel + token bucket per cgroup.
lee: cost note: shaping increases CPU overhead; watch host CPU and billing. but avoids expensive dedicated pool spin-up if it works.
omar: agree. if shaping reduces p99 by >20% we avoid spinning reserved GPUs for these tenants.
maya: I'll run the probe now against 5 smallest hosts. will post results in 30m.
raj: logging — capture `nvidia-smi dmon -s u` and `sar -n DEV 1 60` for baseline.
infra-bot: probe started: nic-shaping-probe-2049876543 on hosts [i-0a1b2c, i-0a1b2d, i-0a1b2e]
maya: initial 10m: p99 dropped 18% on two hosts, 5% on others. disk I/O unaffected. attaching logs.
sylvia: good signal. what's the CPU overhead?
maya: CPU overhead ~3-4% on the shaped hosts. packet retrans consistent lower.
lee: that looks promising. next step: roll shaping to 25% of pool users, monitor regressions, then decide if we make it default or add soft quota on batch size.
raj: can we add a fallback in routing: if tenant batch size > threshold route to dedicated pool? we have routing knobs.
omar: yes we can do canary policy: `if large_batch and pool_shared then prefer dedicated if available`.
maya: created follow-up ticket infra#724: evaluate shaping + routing fallback for large-batch tenants (assign: maya, omar, sylvia). ETA: EOW.
infra-bot: ticket created: infra-724 (https://github.com/redwood/infra/issues/724)
lee: thanks, everyone. keep triangle updates in this thread :thumbsup: 
maya: closing probe thread, will reopen if we see regressions.
